passages.p1:
Cities are often several degrees warmer than the countryside around them, a pattern known as the urban heat island. Concrete and asphalt soak up sunlight during the day and release it slowly through the night, so the hottest neighbourhoods rarely cool down before the next morning.

The burden is not shared equally. Poorer settlements tend to have fewer trees, denser construction and roofs of metal or asbestos sheets, and their residents can seldom afford air-conditioning. Planting trees is the remedy most often proposed, and shade does lower surface temperatures sharply. But trees need space, water and years to mature, and in the most crowded areas there is little room for them. Reflective 'cool roofs', better ventilation in building design and the protection of existing ponds and lakes can act faster.

A city that wants to protect its most vulnerable residents from heat will therefore need a mix of measures, chosen street by street rather than announced as a single programme.
passages.p2:
When employers enrol workers in a pension plan automatically and let them opt out, far more workers end up saving than when joining requires filling in a form. The choice on offer is identical in both cases; only the starting point differs. Economists who once assumed that people weigh every option carefully have had to accept that inertia, procrastination and a dislike of paperwork shape many decisions.

Governments looking for cheap ways to improve behaviour have welcomed this finding. Yet it carries a caution. A default works because most people do not examine it, which means a poorly chosen default — a contribution rate that is too low, or a fund with high fees — will also be accepted without question. The power to set defaults is therefore a responsibility, and those who design them must be held to account for the choices they quietly make on behalf of others.
passages.p3:
Children learn to read most easily in a language they already speak. When the language of the classroom is unfamiliar, the early years are spent decoding words whose meaning is not understood, and many children fall behind before they have had a fair chance. Studies from several countries show that pupils who begin in their home language and add a second language gradually often end up stronger in both.

Such programmes are not simple to run. A single district may contain speakers of many languages, textbooks may not exist in all of them, and teachers trained to teach in them are scarce. Parents, too, sometimes resist, believing that early exposure to a dominant language is the surest route to good jobs. Policy must therefore reckon with practical limits and with parents' aspirations, not only with what the research recommends.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best reflects the central idea of the passage?
o: Air-conditioning should be subsidised for poor households.
Reducing urban heat needs a combination of locally suited measures, with attention to the poorest areas.
Urban heat affects all residents of a city in much the same way.
Tree planting is the only lasting solution to urban heat.
questions.e: The passage notes that the poor bear more of the heat, that trees help but are slow and need space, and that other measures act faster. It ends by calling for a mix of measures chosen street by street.

questions.q:
With reference to the passage, the following assumptions have been made:
1. High night-time temperatures are harmful to residents.
2. Cool roofs cost less than planting trees.
Which of the above assumptions is/are valid?
questions.e: The concern that hot neighbourhoods 'rarely cool down' at night, and the aim of protecting vulnerable residents, assume night heat does harm (1). Cool roofs are said to act faster, not to cost less (2 is not assumed).

questions.q: According to the passage, poorer settlements suffer more from heat because they
o: are usually located far from lakes and ponds
have fewer trees, denser buildings and heat-trapping roofs, and little access to cooling
have residents who mostly work outdoors at night
questions.e: The second paragraph lists these features directly: fewer trees, denser construction, metal or asbestos roofs and little money for air-conditioning.

questions.q: The passage suggests that automatic enrolment raises savings mainly because
o: workers are not allowed to opt out
it offers workers better returns than voluntary plans
people tend to stay with whatever option is already selected
questions.e: The choice is the same either way; only the starting point changes. Inertia and dislike of paperwork mean people keep the pre-selected option.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the most logical inference from the passage?
o: Because defaults are rarely questioned, their design deserves careful scrutiny.
Defaults should be abolished because people do not examine them.
Governments should never try to influence people's behaviour.
People decide carefully whenever money is involved.
questions.e: The same inertia that makes good defaults work makes bad ones stick, so the passage calls setting defaults a responsibility for which designers must be held to account.

questions.q:
Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
1. Inertia influences many financial decisions.
2. Workers who are enrolled automatically can still choose not to save.
questions.e: The passage says inertia and procrastination shape many decisions (1), and automatic enrolment lets workers opt out (2).

questions.q: Which one of the following best reflects the central idea of the passage?
o: Children should be taught only in their home language throughout school.
Starting school in the home language helps learning, but putting it into practice involves real difficulties.
Parents always know best which language their children should study in.
Research on language in education gives no clear answers.
questions.e: The first paragraph gives the benefit of home-language teaching; the second lists the practical and social obstacles that policy must take into account.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT mentioned in the passage as an obstacle to home-language teaching?
o: Lack of textbooks in some languages
Children's inability to learn two languages
Many languages spoken within one district
questions.e: The passage says children who start in the home language often become stronger in both languages, so learning two languages is not an obstacle. The other three are listed.

questions.q: A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above its cost price and then allows a discount of 15% on the marked price. What is his profit per cent?
questions.e: Cost 100 → marked 140 → selling 140 × 0.85 = 119. Profit 19%.

questions.q: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours and pipe B in 15 hours, while pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 hours. If all three are opened together on an empty tank, in how many hours will it be full?
questions.e: Net rate = 1/12 + 1/15 − 1/20 = (5 + 4 − 3)/60 = 1/10 of the tank per hour, so 10 hours.

questions.q: The average of five consecutive odd numbers is 27. What is the largest of them?
questions.e: For consecutive odd numbers the average is the middle one, 27. The numbers are 23, 25, 27, 29, 31.

questions.q: How many integers from 1 to 300 (both inclusive) are divisible by 4 or 6?
questions.e: Divisible by 4: 75; by 6: 50; by both (by 12): 25. 75 + 50 − 25 = 100.

questions.q: A train 150 m long passes completely over a platform 250 m long in 20 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
The ratio of the present ages of A and B is 5 : 3. After 6 years the ratio will be 7 : 5. What is A's present age in years?
The simple interest on a sum for 3 years at 8% per annum is ₹1,440. What is the compound interest on the same sum for 2 years at the same rate, compounded annually?
What is the unit digit of 7⁹⁵?
questions.e: Unit digits of powers of 7 repeat as 7, 9, 3, 1. 95 leaves remainder 3 on division by 4, so the unit digit is 3.

questions.q: A committee of 3 is to be chosen from 5 men and 4 women. In how many ways can it be done if the committee must include at least one woman?
questions.e: All committees: C(9, 3) = 84. All-men committees: C(5, 3) = 10. With at least one woman: 84 − 10 = 74.

questions.q:
Statements:
All doctors are graduates.
Some graduates are singers.
Conclusions:
I. Some doctors are singers.
II. Some singers are graduates.
Which of the conclusions follows/follow from the statements?
o: Both Conclusion I and Conclusion II
Neither Conclusion I nor Conclusion II
questions.e: 'Some graduates are singers' converts to 'Some singers are graduates' (II). The singing graduates need not include any doctor, so I does not follow.

questions.q: In a code, the value of a word is the sum of the positions of its letters in the alphabet. CAT = 24 and DOG = 26. What is the value of BIRD?
Ravi walks 10 m towards North, turns right and walks 6 m, turns right again and walks 4 m, then turns left and walks 2 m. How far is he from the starting point, and in which direction?
questions.e: North 10 → (0, 10); right (East) 6 → (6, 10); right (South) 4 → (6, 6); left (East) 2 → (8, 6). Distance √(64 + 36) = 10 m, towards the North-East.

questions.q: Five friends P, Q, R, S and T sit in a row facing North. R sits at the extreme left end. P sits exactly in the middle. Q sits immediately to the right of P. S does not sit next to R. Who sits at the extreme right end?
questions.e: R _ P Q _ leaves places 2 and 5 for S and T. S cannot be next to R, so S is at place 5 and T at place 2: R T P Q S.

questions.q: Pointing to a man, Meena said, "His mother is the only daughter of my father." How is the man related to Meena?
questions.e: The only daughter of Meena's father is Meena herself, so the man's mother is Meena: he is her son.

questions.q: If 1 March of a year is a Tuesday, what day of the week is 1 June of the same year?
questions.e: From 1 March to 1 June is 31 + 30 + 31 = 92 days = 13 weeks + 1 day. One day after Tuesday is Wednesday.

questions.q: Which product had the highest percentage growth in sales from 2023 to 2024?
questions.e: Growth: P 30/120 = 25%; Q fell by 10%; R 40/80 = 50%; S 10/100 = 10%. R is highest.

questions.q: By what percentage did the total sales of the four products rise from 2023 to 2024?
